subject: Proposal: Azure Private Offer packaging & channel uplift for Nimbus
messages:
From: Rob Walker <rob.walker@join-nimbus.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nimbus.com>, Nimbus Procurement <procurement@nimbus.com>
Date: 2027-05-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Azure private offer — ask on list price floor and partner uplift

Hannah,

Thanks for the demo earlier. Nimbus is evaluating a 12-month private offering on Azure (we want to sell as part of our managed analytics stack). Two asks from Procurement and our channel ops:

- Can Redwood do a list-price floor at 30% off retail for the private offer (we need room to resell)?
- We need a channel uplift / reseller pass-through calculation so our distributor gets a 10-15% margin without impacting Redwood's committed revenue targets.

Also, can you include a one-off onboarding credit and call that out separately in the PO? Procurement will need a single-line net price to put into their system.

Appreciate a quick sketch of options so we can shortlist before the legal review.

—Rob
Nimbus Analytics
[Attachment: Nimbus_pricing_requirements.txt (1KB, text)]

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: Rob Walker <rob.walker@join-nimbus.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-27T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — ask on list price floor and partner uplift

Rob — thanks, this is helpful. High-level response and two packaging options below. I attached a pricing sheet and a channel-margin model for transparency.

Quick take: we can support a 30% list-price floor as a private-offer anchor with two recommended ways to structure the reseller uplift without eroding committed revenue:

Option A — "Pass-through rebate":
- Redwood lists at 30% off retail for Nimbus (customer-facing price).
- Redwood pays a rebate to Nimbus post-invoice based on net usage (example model in channel_margin_model_v2.xlsx).
- Pros: preserves Redwood commit, simple for Procurement to see a net price.
- Cons: requires a reconciled true-up (monthly or quarterly).

Option B — "Reseller SKU with embedded margin":
- Create a reseller SKU with slightly higher list price to give Nimbus an embedded 12% margin at invoicing.
- Redwood recognizes revenue on the reseller SKU; commit mapping handled via SKU mapping to the same offer.
- Pros: simpler ops for Nimbus, fewer retro true-ups.
- Cons: slightly higher apparent list price; needs marketplace SKU mapping.

Onboarding credit: we can include a one-time credit as a separate line item (SOW credit) and show the net price on the single-line PO export.

Next steps I suggest:
1) I can run a short margin waterfall (Ben helped build the draft model) for both options given your expected first-year usage.
2) If Nimbus prefers A, we’ll prepare a monthly reconciliation cadence and a short Ops note for accounting.
3) If Nimbus prefers B, we’ll coordinate SKU mapping with Marketplace ops (Marcus to review feasibility).

Attachments: AZ_PrivateOffer_PricingSheet_v3.pdf (pricing matrix + examples), channel_margin_model_v2.xlsx (waterfall).

If possible, send a target first-year ARR estimate (top-line usage) and whether the reseller will be an authorized distributor or a direct sub-seller. I can turn this into a numeric example by EOD.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: AZ_PrivateOffer_PricingSheet_v3.pdf (24KB, PDF)]

From: Rob Walker <rob.walker@join-nimbus.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nimbus.com>, Nimbus Procurement <procurement@nimbus.com>
Date: 2027-05-28T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private offer — ask on list price floor and partner uplift

Hannah — thanks for the clear options. Procurement prefers Option A (pass-through rebate) because it produces a clear net line on the PO. A couple follow-ups / constraints from our side:

- Can we fix the true-up cadence to monthly and cap the reconciliation lag at 45 days?
- The distributor requires that the rebate payment be visible on their side as a separate remittance (they won't accept an embedded margin).
- We need a simple SOW line for the onboarding credit (we expect a $25k one-time).

I've pasted Procurement's sample PO field requirements below (they want a single numeric net price + separate SOW credit ID). If you can provide the net monthly price and a projected first-year total for the model, we can route for stamp.

On DocuSign: procurement prefers a single DocuSign envelope per private offer (they can’t accept multiple envelopes per SKU). If you can generate that once we agree on numbers we can sign quickly.

—Rob

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-28T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Nimbus prefers pass-through rebate (Option A) — need finance + ops signoff

Team — Nimbus (potential $1.2M first-year ARR estimate, per Rob on the call) favors Option A (monthly pass-through rebate; onboarding credit $25k one-time). Key asks from Nimbus: monthly true-up (45-day cap) and separate remittance visibility for the distributor.

Questions for finance/ops:
- Ben: can finance run the rebate payment cadence & ledger entry treatment so commit recognition isn't impacted? We need to ensure reseller rebates don't reduce recognized committed revenue for Redwood (they must net against channel expense line).
- Irene: can Marketplace ops support exposing a single net price to Nimbus Procurement while we handle the rebate as a post-invoice remittance? If not, what is the operational gap and ETA to close it?
- Marcus: pls confirm SKU mapping complexity for a pass-through approach — will this require a new reseller SKU or can we use the private-offer mapping and then reconcile via the channel model?

I've attached the model that includes a monthly waterfall and a sample PO net-price calculation. If we can close finance/ops questions today, I’ll send a numeric example back to Nimbus and request signature via DocuSign.

Attachments: channel_margin_model_v2.xlsx (waterfall), Nimbus_SOW_draft.docx (SOW line draft).

Thanks — Hannah

[Attachment: channel_margin_model_v2.xlsx (18KB, XLSX)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-29T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Nimbus prefers pass-through rebate (Option A) — need finance + ops signoff

Hannah / team — reviewed the model. Finance signs off on Option A with one change: rebate should be recorded to channel expense and tied to a monthly true-up ledger; commit recognition will remain against gross invoice as long as the rebate is documented as a separate remit. That satisfies accounting as long as procurement sees a single net price on the PO and we issue a separate remittance file to the distributor.

Operational notes:
- Marcus: please coordinate SKU mapping as a private-offer mapping (no new reseller SKU required). Confirm by close of day tomorrow so we can generate the DocuSign envelope.
- Irene: ops should prepare a short remittance CSV template (fields: invoice_id, remit_amount, distributor_id) — we’ll attach it to the monthly reconciliation.

Hannah: once Marcus confirms, approve the numeric example and I’ll authorize the onboarding credit ($25k) and greenlight DocuSign.

—Ben
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: approval_note.txt (500B, text)]
